statement: A fish tank is 50 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm tall. It is filled to the top using a jug that holds 2 litres. How many full jugs of water are needed?

choices.misconception: I found the tank holds 60 litres and forgot that each jug holds 2 litres.
I thought 1 litre is 100 cubic centimetres, so I found 600 litres and divided by 2.
I thought 1 litre is 1 cubic centimetre, so I divided 60,000 by 2.
I found the tank holds 60 litres and multiplied by 2 instead of dividing.

hints: How many cubic centimetres make one litre?
Find the volume of the tank in cubic centimetres, convert it to litres using 1 litre = 1,000 cubic centimetres, then share it out into 2-litre jugs.
The tank holds 50 x 30 x 40 = 60,000 cubic centimetres.

solutions.reliable: The tank holds 50 x 30 x 40 = 60,000 cubic centimetres. One litre is 1,000 cubic centimetres, so that is 60 litres. Each jug holds 2 litres, so 60 / 2 = 30 jugs are needed. The transferable idea: get every quantity into the same unit before dividing, and know that a litre is the volume of a 10 cm cube.
solutions.elegant: A 2-litre jug is 2,000 cubic centimetres, and 60,000 / 2,000 = 30.

whyOnTest: Volume conversion is where students slip, because a litre is 1,000 cubic centimetres, not 100 and not 1.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
